 Order

This appeal is filed under Section 30 of the Employees Compensation Ac t, 1923 being aggrieved of award dated 04.02.2021 passed by learned Commissioner under Workmen Compensation Act/Labour Court Khandwa in Claim Case No.10/WC NF Act/2015 on the ground that Tractor bearing registration No. MP 10AB 0898 owned by Sheikh Mukeem was insured with the appellant National Insurance Company, trolley was insured with Oriental Insurance Company and it was owned by Sheikh Kaleem s/o Sheikh Gulam Nabi.

Admittedly, accident took place on 09.01.2015 when deceased Sanjay, Narendra, Ramdas were travelling in the trolley along with the driver of the tractor namely, Anil, and when trolley turned turtle they sustained grievous injuries, resulting in death.

It is submitted that number of the trolley could not be explained and, therefore, it was found that the trolley which met with an accident was not insured with the Oriental Insurance Company but learned Tribunal implicated National Insurance Company as the insurer of the tractor.
Smt. Amrit Kaur Ruprah, in her turn, submits that it has come on record that injured- Narendra was employee of Manish s/o Anokhilal Sapner.
He had hired tractor from Sheikh Mukeem Khan.
Coverage under the policy under the Workmen Compensation Act is for an employee of Sheikh Mukeem Khan and not for the employee of Manish.
It is submitted that it has come in evidence that injured- Narendra was drawing salary from Manish i.e. Manish was his employer.
Therefore, Insurance Company should have been exonerated and award should have been passed against Manish and Sheikh Mukeem instead of the Insurance Company.

S h r i Swapnil Khare reading Section 12(1) of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923 submits that even if a work is outsourced then employee of such outsource agency is to be vicariously compensated by the principle employer and, therefore, claimant is entitled to be indemnified by the Insurance Company.

sentences.text: Shri Gulab Chand Sohane, in his turn, submits that Oriental Insurance Company has been rightly exonerated, no indulgence is required in the matter.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, it is evident that tractor was hired by Manish.
There is no iota of dispute in regard to this.
It is also admitted position that Ex.D-1 insured trolley bearing No.MP 10 A 9604.

Thus, it was necessary for the owner to approve that the trolley which met with an accident was under insurance with Oriental Insurance Company,
but this fact could not be proved, therefore, exoneration of Oriental Insurance Company, insurer of the trolley cannot be said to be arbitrary and illegal.

The question which arises is that whether deceased as an employee of Manish who had hired tractor of Sheikh Mukeem for his own work i.e. transportation of sand can be said to be employee of Sheikh Mukeem whose tractor was insured under the Farmers Package Policy for the purpose of transport of sand.
As per the definition of an employee mentioned in Section 2 (dd), means a person recruited as driver, helper, mechanic, cleaner or in any other capacity in connection with a motor vehicle.

Thus,
it is evident that onus is on the claimant to have proved that he was appointed in connection with the motor vehicle.

Employer is defined in Section 2(e) as includes any body of persons whether incorporated or not and any managing agent of an employer and the legal representative of a deceased employer, and, when the services of an employee are temporarily lent or let on hire to another person by the person with whom the employee has entered into a contract of service or apprenticeship, means such other person while the employee is working for him.

When these definitions are read together it is evident that in absence of any averment that injured-Narendra was hired by Sheikh Mukeem owner of the tractor, he cannot be deemed to be an employee of Sheikh Mukeem to have coverage under the Workmen Compensation Act and,
accordingly, the impugned award having been passed without having regard to the provisions contained in the employees compensation Act, 1923 deserves to be set aside qua Insurance Company and is set aside.
However, it is directed that owner of the tractor Sheikh Mukeem and the hirer Manish shall be jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award.
In above terms, appeal is disposed of.
Record of the Tribunal be sent back.
